editorial:
Imagine being twelve years old and trying to figure out your dad after he spends years in prison. You get to see the world through the eyes of a young boy in Watts, California, who is just looking for some love and attention. The movie feels very real and grounded, but it has a strange twist because the kid starts seeing things that aren't there. You'll see airplanes and old Greek gods floating around his neighborhood, which makes the whole story feel like a dream and a reality at the same time. It is a touching look at family and growing up in a tough spot.

The acting is the best part here because the kid feels like a real person, not just a movie character. While the story moves a bit slow in the middle, the weird visions keep you interested in what happens next. If you like stories about fathers and sons, you should definitely check this one out. It looks amazing in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, but if you are a movie collector, you should grab the 4K Blu-ray to see all the detail in those Greek god scenes.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, the boy realizes the Greek gods were actually his way of dealing with the sadness of his father being gone. He finally has a heart-to-heart talk with his dad, and they both cry and hug. The visions disappear once he feels safe and loved again. It ends with them walking together through the neighborhood, showing that their relationship is finally starting to heal and they can move forward.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves heartfelt family stories and a bit of fantasy.
